name: Gemeente Den Haag
description: Gemeente Den Haag's own design tokens: green buttons, blue links, a white page header.
provenance: the pinned @gemeente-denhaag token CSS vendored under scripts/sources/denhaag/, EUPL-1.2, Gemeente Den Haag
_comment_source: WHY THIS SET IS SOURCED AND THE OTHER SEVEN BRIDGE-ZERO SETS ARE NOT.
The coverage audit reported 8 bridged sets declaring none of the 87
them have no published token package here, so completing them would mean
choosing roughly 35 ramp steps for a municipality's house style. Den Haag is
the exception: scripts/sources/denhaag/ already holds its pinned token CSS,
vendored for scripts/generate-denhaag-bridge.mjs and annotated EUPL-1.2 in
REUSE.toml. So every value below is read off that source, and the ones with
no basis in it are left out rather than chosen.
WHAT IS LEFT OUT, and why, so nobody has to re-derive it:
- 35 of the 87 bridge names. The source declares no --utrecht-heading-N-color,
no -font-weight for any heading, no --utrecht-heading-6-* at all, no
--utrecht-form-input-* and no --utrecht-separator-*. They keep the bridge
fallback, which is an --nldesign-* token this set declares.
- the pink ramp (4 steps), extra-limegreen and extra-purple. Den Haag
publishes no magenta, lime or purple family. The role layer keeps its own
there and the generator reports it.
COLOURS ARE CONVERTED, NOT CHOSEN. The source states its palette in hsl();
this file states the same colours as 8-bit sRGB hex, because the contrast
engine (ContrastService::parseColor) reads hex and rgb() and returns null for
hsl(). Leaving hsl() in would make every Den Haag pair in the contrast report
unmeasurable instead of passing. The conversion is round-to-nearest on each
channel, and here is the whole table so it can be rechecked:
_comment_ramp: The role layer aliases --vng-color-* / --tilburg-color-*, so re-branding it
means replacing that ramp. Den Haag publishes five steps per hue and the role
layer wants eleven greys, so the grey rows state the rule they follow:
take the declared Den Haag neutral whose own hsl lightness is nearest the
slot's, and never compute a step in between. That lands five Den Haag greys on
ten slots, two slots each, with warmgrey-1 on gray-50. gray-400 is the one
close call: 82% against the slot’s 66%, with grey-3 at 48% one point further.
The hue ramps map one for one, lightest to darkest, so denhaag blue-1 lands on
blue-100 and blue-5 on blue-500. Den Haag red-5 and the pink family have no

gray-200.from: denhaag-color-grey-1 (lightness 95% against the slot’s 91%; grey-2 at 82% is further)

gray-400.from: denhaag-color-grey-2 (lightness 82% against the slot’s 66%; grey-3 at 48% is one point further)

gray-950.from: denhaag-color-grey-5 (lightness 18% against the slot’s 11%; black at 0% is further)

extra-yellow.from: denhaag-color-ocher-3 (ocher is Den Haag’s yellow family, and 3 is its mid step)

code-background-color.from: denhaag-color-grey-1 (the lightest declared neutral surface, which is what the role layer used here)

_comment_literal_overrides: Colours the role layer hard-codes inside a component declaration instead of

value. Each one is replaced by the Den Haag step that holds the same ROLE
where Den Haag states one, and the same hue where it does not.

_comment_upstream_overrides: Four deliberate departures from the source, each with the reason the run
The two font families are licensing. TheSans and TheMix are LucasFonts
retail faces that Den Haag licenses; this repository may not redistribute
either. The stack keeps the licensed family first, so an instance that has it
renders in it, and adds the self-hosted Fira Sans behind it. token-sets.json
carries the licence position an administrator acts on, the same way duo does
The two tilburg-prefixed tokens are colours the role layer states as literals
that no ramp entry can reach, because Den Haag publishes no purple and no
pink. Pointing them at the Den Haag token that holds the same role is better
than leaving a VNG focus ring and a VNG pink badge in a Den Haag set.

--denhaag-typography-sans-serif-font-fam.reason: TheSans is a licensed LucasFonts face and cannot ship here. Fira Sans follows it as the self-hosted stand-in.

--denhaag-typography-sans-serif-alternat.reason: TheMix is a licensed LucasFonts face and cannot ship here. Fira Sans follows it as the self-hosted stand-in.

--tilburg-focus-outline-color.reason: Den Haag's own focus colour is ocher-5, which it states in --denhaag-focus-border-color. The role layer's purple has no Den Haag counterpart.

--tilburg-status-badge-background-color.reason: Den Haag gives --utrecht-badge-background-color grey-1. The role layer uses a pink Den Haag does not publish.

_comment_semantic: The --nldesign-* layer Nextcloud chrome and the Portaliq site renderer read.
Every value names the Den Haag token it came from, and every source is a role
Den Haag states in its own token CSS:
THE THREE THAT HAVE NO ROLE OF THEIR OWN IN THE SOURCE.
primary-light-hover is green-1 again, because green-1 is the only green Den
Haag ever fills a surface with. Its one use of green-2 is a border, on
--denhaag-floating-contact-switch-border-color, so a hover wash made from it
would be a colour Den Haag does not paint. The visible cost is a hover state
that matches the rest state; the cost of the alternative was measured and is
worse. Deriving the dark variant with green-2 here pushed
--nldesign-color-primary to near-black #111111, because the repair loop could
not reach 4.5:1 for primary sitting on the lightened green-2 wash.
error-hover is red-5, the next declared step down. button-primary-border is
green-3, the same value as the fill, because the source declares no
THE HEADER IS WHITE, which is the one change a reader will notice. Den Haag
sets --denhaag-page-header-background-color to white and its own side
navigation to grey-4 on white. The set this replaces painted the Nextcloud
header green, which no Den Haag token asks for. No headerIconFilter follows,
because a light header wants the defaults layer’s dark icons.
_comment_typography: The family is Den Haag’s own, with the repository’s self-hosted stand-in
behind it. No scale or weight steps are listed, because the source already
states both and the generator emits them verbatim in section A as
under a second prefix would give one type scale two names.

_comment: Den Haag publishes exactly one radius token, --denhaag-border-radius: 3px,
and gives it to the button, the textbox, the badge and the select. So every
role below is that one value. pill is the role layer’s own lozenge geometry
and is not a Den Haag value.
